chapter: Pictures and memories of her father
title: Serenading at 2 a.m. and favorite pieces
summary: Father, Albert Glenny and violinist Wendell MacNeil serenaded the family at night with mutes; his favorites included Night and Day and Sweet Mystery of Life.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: You know what was wonderful? I guess I must have been a little girl about, oh, about nine years old. And my daddy used to have Albert Glenny and...who was daddy called? MacNeil.
Thomas MacNeil. Wendell MacNeil was his name. Wendell MacNeil. And my daddy and Albert Glenny. And they used to wake us up with serenaders. Two o'clock in the morning.
I thought I needed to win that phrase.
Is he a guitar player, MacNeil? No, violinist. Violin, I forgot.
He's in Chicago. I don't know if he's living or not. That's where he went to.
When I was a little kid, I was playing with Woody Symphony.

He played a sweet violin. But that was so sweet. You know, in the early hours of the morning, and they had their mutes. My daddy would use the mute in his horn. Yeah. And that was so sweet to hear that music at two o'clock in the morning. I never did forget that.
What kind of pieces were they? Something slow or what were they like? Do you remember what?
Well, it would be something popular of the time, you know. But I can't remember just what pieces he played. But his favorite, my daddy's favorite piece was Night and Day.

And, uh, Come to, uh, what is it? Oh, Come to Me? Yeah. Oh, Come to Me. Always on the Eyes. Oh, Come to Me. He used to love to play that. He played that with that mute. And, uh, and, um, uh, what was the name of that piece again? I can't think of it. As much as I'd like to say it. Our Sweet Mystery of Life. Oh, yeah.
The Victor Herbert, I used to play that. Oh, yeah. My daddy played.
Well, I used to play the piano. Why is it then? And we used to play together.
